subject.title: [Bug]: Task and Memory Recall Is Often Too Weak to Trust Across Real Conversations

question: Should OpenClaw make reliable project/task memory a default core behavior, document it as a workspace/plugin pattern, or split this umbrella into narrower memory engine and session-recall fixes first?
rationale: Current main has partial primitives but no established default contract for project/task state, and broader recall changes privacy, defaults, and product boundaries that automation should not choose.

options.title: Keep umbrella and split tracks
options.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical reliability report while maintainers create focused child work for task-state capture, session recall, ranking, diagnostics, and live QA proof.

options.title: Route cross-session recall to narrower issues
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/99611, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/51386, and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/53550 for transcript recall while preserving this issue only for project/task mutation semantics.

options.title: Document as workspace pattern
options.body: Treat default task memory as a documented workspace or plugin pattern if maintainers decide core should not own a canonical project/task state system.

recommendation.title: Keep umbrella and split tracks
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the canonical reliability report while maintainers create focused child work for task-state capture, session recall, ranking, diagnostics, and live QA proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Their open related proposal already frames the same-assistant recall product boundary that must align with any broader default memory decision.
